Anchor migration correctness, waiver identity across rounds and PRs, and harvest grouping all depend on the exact algorithm, and waivers must remain matchable across cr versions, so an undocumented choice becomes a silent compatibility contract.
suggestion: Define each normalisation in the spec text: for anchors, strip trailing whitespace, collapse internal runs of whitespace to one space, drop blank lines, then SHA-256 the joined lines; for summaries and comment bodies, lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation and any embedded path:line tokens before hashing. Record the normalisation version in the waiver record so a future change is detectable rather than silently invalidating stored waivers.

finding: 'Open' is used normatively without a definition over the §9.1 state set: §9.3.2 classifies 'each open thread' as untouched, touched, or stale, and §10.2.3 accepts a claim that 'has an open unimplemented-claim record'. §9.1.2 names only `fixed` and `accepted` as terminal, which would make `discarded` and `regressed` open. Recheck and convergence tests both depend on the exact set.
suggestion: Define 'open' in §1.1 or §9.1 as an explicit list of states and use that list in §9.3.2, §10.2.3, and §10.2.4 rather than restating it.

finding: §9.3.4 requires cr to `Compute the delta diff since the last reviewed head`, but §9.2 exists precisely because force-pushes happen. After a rebase or amend the previous head is often not an ancestor of the new head and may be unreachable and garbage-collected, in which case the delta is either meaningless or not computable at all. §3.4.1 defines the review diff against the PR merge base instead, so the two sections use different bases with no statement of which wins or how they are reconciled.
suggestion: Specify detection and fallback: if the previous head is missing or is not an ancestor of the new head, record the round as a rebase, fall back to a full merge-base diff for clustering, and mark units that were reviewed in prior rounds so effort is not repeated. State that anchor migration per §9.2 remains the mechanism for carrying findings across, independent of which diff base was used.

finding: The evidence-grade discipline of §6.2 governs raising a concern but nothing governs closing one. §9.4.1 lets the agent record `fixed` on judgement alone, §9.5.1 then resolves the GitHub thread — an outward-facing act asserting to the author and to every later reader that the concern was addressed — and §9.5.2 requires only evidence text, unstructured prose that cr cannot check. A record originally graded `probed` may be closed without re-running its probe, even though §5.5.3 already establishes that only a same-head probe counts as evidence.
suggestion: Give verification outcomes the same grades as findings: a `probed` record MUST be closed by a same-head re-run of its probe with the opposite result, a `cited` record by a re-resolved citation at the new head, and anything else is `argued` and MUST be surfaced to the human as a reply-question rather than resolving the thread. Store the closing grade on the record and report it in §10.1.

finding: §5.4.2 requires `cr` to 'place the test in the sandbox, run it, remove it', without saying where the file is placed, how it is named, what happens if a file of that name already exists, or how the runner discovers it. Placement is exactly what makes a gap probe reproducible under §2.1.1, and removal of the wrong file would write into the sandbox worktree unexpectedly, so a test can assert nothing about either step.
suggestion: Add a per-profile probe test directory with a stated default, require a generated name that includes the probe id so collisions are impossible, and require the command to fail with exit code 3 rather than overwrite an existing file.

finding: §6.3.3 introduces `--allow-argued-findings`, but the flag appears in no command row in §11, is absent from the §11.1 global-flag table, and §10.3's list of required round counts has no slot for its use even though §6.3.3 requires that use to be `recorded in the round`.
suggestion: Add the flag to §11.1 or to the specific command rows that accept it (most plausibly `cr record` only), and add `argued findings allowed` to the counts §10.3 requires every round to record.

finding: The numbered list in §7.4 is numbered 1, 2, 2, 3, 4 — the rule-scoped-waiver item and the "Waived findings MUST be dropped before drafting" item are both item 2. Numbered items in this spec are load-bearing references (§7.4.1 is cited as the waiver-key requirement, §2.6.1.3 as the grading rule), and tp's backward pass matches acceptance criteria to numbered items, so the duplicate makes one requirement unaddressable by number and can let it be silently dropped from task coverage.
suggestion: Renumber §7.4 as 1 through 5.

finding: The numbered list in §7.4 runs 1, 2, 2, 3, 4 — the rule-scoped waiver item and the drop-before-drafting item are both numbered 2. Beyond being ambiguous to cite, this breaks the project's backward-coverage pass, which requires every numbered list item in a spec to map to a task acceptance by position. Separately, §7.4.3 offers `cr waivers remove <id>` while §7.4.1's waiver key is a triple and no waiver schema anywhere defines an `id` field.
suggestion: Renumber §7.4 to 1..5, and add a short waiver schema table naming `id`, `class`, `anchor_hash`, `summary_hash`, `rule`, `path_prefix`, `pr`, `round` and `reason`, so `cr waivers remove <id>` has a defined target.

finding: §8.2.3 requires the leading whitespace of the first replaced line to be preserved unless the suggestion explicitly changes indentation. cr cannot decide whether a suggestion explicitly intends an indentation change without forming an opinion about intent, which §2.1 and P5 forbid. As written the clause is unimplementable, and its failure mode is a posted suggestion that produces broken indentation the moment the author clicks apply.
suggestion: Replace the intent test with a declared one: a record MAY carry `suggestion_reindent: true`, and without it cr MUST preserve the original leading whitespace and MUST fail validation with exit 1 (per §8.2.4, naming the record id) when the suggestion's first line differs in indentation.

finding: §8.5.1 requires an unconfirmed `cr post` to print the payload and exit 0 — the same exit code as a successful post. Combined with §12.1, which makes output JSON whenever stdout is not a terminal, the dry run's default consumer is the agent's pipe rather than a human's screen, and no caller can distinguish previewed from posted by exit status alone.
suggestion: Keep exit 0 but require an explicit discriminator in both output modes (posted: false alongside dry_run: true in JSON, and a prominent banner in text) and state that the dry-run output MUST name the draft file the human is expected to have read before re-running with --confirm.

finding: §9.2 gives an anchor a `side` field, implying `LEFT` anchors on deleted lines are representable, but no behaviour is defined for them. §6.1.2 requires a finding's anchor to "resolve to a line in the current head", which a LEFT anchor by definition does not; §9.2.1 migrates anchors by "searching the new file for the content hash", which a deleted line will never match, so every LEFT anchor degrades to `stale-anchor` on the first head change; and §8.2.1 restricts suggestions to the `RIGHT` side without saying whether a LEFT-anchored comment may be posted at all.
suggestion: Either restrict anchors to `RIGHT` in §9.2 and drop the `side` field, or define LEFT-anchor semantics explicitly: how §6.1.2 is satisfied, how §9.2.1 migration behaves (presumably match against the base file at the new merge base), and that suggestions are rejected for LEFT anchors.
